tia-cs: Pasting a customer report: Acme sees JSON streams truncated ~30% of the time when routed through their F5 load balancer. They say the final '}' or ']' is missing and the payload is parse-invalid. Started after they updated LB idle timeout last week. They supplied curl + sample output and our headers.

jess-support: Can you paste the exact curl and headers they used? Is there another proxy between them and us?

tia-cs: Here is the curl they ran (redacted):
```
curl -v -N \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?mode=structured_json"
```
Sample truncated tail they sent: "... \n \"items\": [ { ... }, { ... } ] \n\"meta\": { \"count\": 12 }"  <-- missing final closing brace in about 1/3 of responses.

mohit-runtime: Assigning to eng-runtime to investigate. @ellie-oncall can you check edge/transport logs for the reported times? My initial hunch: client (or LB) is closing connection mid-stream (FIN) so final chunk never reaches client. :eyes: 

ellie-oncall: Checked our edge logs for the timestamps they provided (2024-10-11T15:22:03Z etc). Observed TCP FIN from 10.20.30.40 (customer LB) at ~29s into stream while our backend had already written remaining bytes. We also see a 502/TCP reset in the path. Attaching tcpdump snippet (redacted):
```
14:22:31.123456 IP 10.20.30.40.443 > 172.18.0.10.54012: Flags [F.], seq 12345, ack 67890, win 512
14:22:31.123457 IP 172.18.0.10.54012 > 10.20.30.40.443: RST, seq 1, win 0
```

mohit-runtime: That matches a mid-stream client close. Two observations: (1) customer says changing curl --no-keepalive reduces failures, (2) they stream ~10-15k tokens (multi-chunk). If the LB enforces an idle or response window and issues FIN mid-body, we can end up with truncated JSON. Need repro with their LB config.

tia-cs: Customer reported "--no-keepalive" reduced failures to ~5% but didn't eliminate them. They also said enabling proxy-buffering on F5 made it worse. They use newline-delimited JSON objects in structured_json mode.

jess-support: Do we currently flush final chunk/closing bracket in a separate write that could lose ordering if socket returns EPIPE? If backend write fails we should try best-effort to retry or mark as partial with clear error. Right now we just surface truncated body.

mohit-runtime: Quick repro plan: I'll run a local haproxy with their timeouts and replay a large stream from staging runtime. If haproxy sends FIN to client while backend still streaming, our runtime's async write may hit EPIPE and drop the rest. Will instrument write return codes and add a sync-flush-on-close guard.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-10-12T18:12:03: success to staging: runtime v1.43.2 (instrumentation + sync-flush-on-close guard) :rocket:

mohit-runtime: I reproduced with haproxy and the customer's settings. Sequence: backend writes chunk 123, kernel queues, LB hits idle window and sends FIN to client, kernel returns EPIPE on subsequent write, our runtime currently treats that as done and doesn't propagate a clear truncation signal. Patch adds: detect EPIPE on write, log full dump of buffered bytes, attempt single synchronous send of queued bytes (best-effort) and mark stream as 'closed-by-client' in logs. This lets us at least give a deterministic error and provide the customer with a clear failure reason.

ellie-oncall: Rolled v1.43.2 to staging, running 10k-stream load test against haproxy config. So far no silent truncations; failures now show explicit 'client_closed_midstream' with payload hash. If staging stays green, recommend we: (a) ask customers to increase LB idle timeout or enable chunked streaming without downstream idle cutoff, (b) add KB article and CS playbook. :thumbsup:

tia-cs: Customer can test in ~30m. I'll coordinate with their infra team (they're willing to increase idle timeout for a narrow test window).

jess-support: After we confirm customer repro/no-repro, please add a support KB: steps to repro, indicators in runtime logs (client_closed_midstream, EPIPE write failure, tcpdump patterns), customer mitigations (increase LB idle timeout, disable proxy buffering, client keepalive options), and internal mitigation (runtime v1.43.2 guard).

jess-support: Also flag this as a potential short-term doc for sales engineering so they can advise customers using F5/NGINX/HAProxy.

(Conversation paused while we wait for customer test.)
